newsitem.title: CANADA: Avenor offers C$3.3 billion ($2.4 billion) for Repap.
newsitem.headline: Avenor offers C$3.3 billion ($2.4 billion) for Repap.

text.p: Avenor Inc. Wednesday offered to buy the troubled pulp and paper company Repap Enterprises Inc. for C$3.3 billion ($2.4 billion), including the assumption of debt, in a deal that would create Canada's second-largest forest products company.
Avenor said it planned to issue 29 million new shares as part of its all-stock offer for Repap Enterprises, which has pulp and coated paper mills in Canada and a large mill in Kimberly, Wis.

In a telephone conference call with reporters, Avenor Chief Executive Paul Gagne said the stock will be issued as part of Avenor's offer to exchange one newly issued Avenor common share for every 4.25 Repap shares.
He said the combined Avenor and Repap will have annual revenues of C$5 billion ($3.7 billion), making it Canada's second biggest pulp and paper maker after MacMillan Bloedel Ltd.

Avenor's Chief Financial Officer Denis Aubin said the value of the common share exchange was C$617 million ($453.6 million), while the total value of the company's offer, including existing Repap debt of C$2.5 billion ($1.8 billion), brings the purchase price to C$3.3 billion.
He said Avenor's common share exchange offer works out to C$5 ($3.76) for each Repap share.
Following the news, Avenor's stock plunged C$2 to C$19.20 ($14.12) and Repap lost C$1.05 to C$4.45 ($3.27), both traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Gagne said Avenor would move "aggressively" to create synergies after the purchase, but he declined to indicate specifically which assets Avenor might divest.

He said that Repap Chairman and Chief Executive George Petty will become a director of Avenor following the acquisition but he declined to elaborate on the future role of Repap's President Stephen Larsen.
The acquisition is expects to be completed by Feb. 28.
